herdr: one place for all agents and workspaces

The problem it solves

With agents, I rarely work on one thing. Three or four projects are in flight, and each agent is either working, waiting for my approval or done. With plain terminal windows or tmux panes I lose track of which is which, and an agent waiting for a yes sits idle until I happen to look.

The general idea

herdr is a terminal workspace manager built for this. It runs inside the terminal I already use and organises work into workspaces, tabs and tiled panes. It recognises coding agents and shows their state in a sidebar, so I see at a glance which workspace needs me. Sessions keep running when I disconnect, like tmux, and plugins extend it.

Examples

The sidebar rows in my herdr.toml show the agent state, the workspace, the git branch and the project status:

[ui.sidebar.spaces]
rows = [
  ["state_icon", "workspace"],
  ["branch", "git_status"],
  [{ token = "$pomodoro", fg = "#f38ba8", bold = true }],
  [{ token = "$openspec", fg = "#89b4fa" }],
]

Keys are bound to plugin actions, for example a fuzzy command bar and Yazi in a split:

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+k"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "herdr-bar.open"
description = "command bar"

Tips from my setup

  • Claude Code reports its state through a small hook, so the sidebar icon reflects what the agent is really doing. A sound or a toast tells me when one finishes.
  • Plugins I use: a command bar to jump between tabs, agents, repositories and branches, a file viewer, Yazi in a split, a diff viewer, a review sidebar, automatic tab names, the Neovim integration, an OpenSpec browser and two of my own, notify and the pomodoro timer.
  • The sidebar stays collapsed by default. I open it when I want the overview and keep the screen for the code otherwise.
  • Other machines in the same place. herdr can save machines and open their workspaces over SSH, which fits the setup from the post about working from anywhere.
  • Agents can read each other's tabs. A skill lets an agent read the last lines of a named tab in its workspace, to check what is failing or stuck there.
  • A clock and a timer in the tab bar, next to a small system monitor.
